The shipped templates DO span 22 as of 2026-08-27 (#52 and #59): TransitionSpanTest and

this pitch, and both pass. They are release gates (./gradlew releaseCheck) rather than part of

Watch the log for [D2-PITCH] and [D2-SPAN]. Every other field in this file is safe to tune.
//floor_cells_per_room_template: How much of a dungeon is AUTHORED rather than procedurally dressed: one prefab-room assembly
attempt per this many cells of a floor's own footprint. 0 turns prefab rooms off entirely
without emptying the pool, which is the only way to A/B them.
A DENSITY, NOT A COUNT, since 2026-09-07. It used to be room_template_attempts_per_floor,
shipped at 4 -- the same four attempts on every floor however big it was. But room COUNT has
always scaled with floor AREA, and a LARGE floor is about three times a MEDIUM one, so the
authored share fell off a cliff as dungeons got bigger. Measured over 300 seeds per tier:
at the old flat 4      at 520 cells/template
Backwards from what anyone wants: the biggest dungeon, where the player sees the most rooms,
felt the most generated. Raising the flat count could not fix it -- at its ceiling of 8, LARGE
still only reached 20.2% while SMALL hit 68.2% and its floors began to crowd.
520 LEVELS THE THREE TIERS at roughly where MEDIUM already was, which is the tier the feel was
judged on. So it raises LARGE and deliberately LOWERS SMALL. Lower this number for more
authored rooms everywhere: ~320 gives ~30%, ~215 gives ~45%. Cost scales with it, because each
attempt is TWO jigsaw assemblies (a probe to measure the rotated footprint, then the placement).
RE-MEASURE, NEVER QUOTE. RoomAssemblyPlacementTest prints the share. A change to room count
moves these figures without anything touching this field, and that has caught this project out
twice already.
//sink_offset: How far the walking plane sits UP into its own floor's slab -- the depth a sunken pit has to
sink into (backlog #3). SHIPPED AT 0, which makes the whole mechanism arithmetically absent.
It is bought from the CEILING, not from the descent. A floor owns exactly floorHeight blocks
either way; sinkOffset just moves the boundary inside that budget, leaving
floorHeight - sinkOffset above the walking plane and sinkOffset below it. So the floor-to-floor
pitch does NOT move and no transition template has to be re-cut to allow pits -- which is the
whole reason pits are separable from the floorHeight raise rather than blocked behind it.
5 as of 2026-08-27, bought by raising floorHeight to 20: a 15-block ceiling budget for
authored rooms, 5 for pits, and a
transition drop of 22. It trades one-for-one against room height, so raising this without
raising floorHeight takes the height straight back out of the rooms; the file fails to load if
it leaves less headroom than a roomHeightBand asks for.
//room_height_bands: UNCHANGED by the floorHeight raise, deliberately (Gottsch, 2026-08-27). The 15-block ceiling
budget is headroom for AUTHORED rooms -- a template may be cut 15 high and now fits. A
PROCEDURAL room stays capped at 10: a tall empty box is a worse room than a short one, and
what makes height worth having is content, which a template has and a rolled room does not.
The slack above a procedural room costs nothing -- unused floor height is unexcavated stone,
not empty volume, and is invisible in play.
The taper itself is #51: the ceiling FALLS as the footprint grows, so a 7x7 may be a shaft
